🔄 Transactions

BLite provides full ACID transaction support with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) for durability and crash recovery. All write operations are async-only since v4.0.0.

Auto-commit (Default Behavior)

By default every write operation (InsertAsync, UpdateAsync, DeleteAsync) is individually auto-committed when no explicit transaction is passed. This is the simplest model and is sufficient for most use cases.

using var db = new AppDbContext("mydb.blite");

// Each operation commits immediately — no transaction needed
await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Alice", Age = 30 });
await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Bob", Age = 25 });

Bulk Insert

var newUsers = new List<User>
{
    new User { Name = "User1", Age = 20 },
    new User { Name = "User2", Age = 21 },
    new User { Name = "User3", Age = 22 }
};

// InsertBulkAsync auto-commits all documents in one WAL write
await db.Users.InsertBulkAsync(newUsers);
💡 About SaveChangesAsync()

SaveChangesAsync() called without a transaction argument is a no-op — it exists only for API compatibility. For atomic multi-operation batches use an explicit transaction (see below) and call SaveChangesAsync(txn) or txn.CommitAsync().

Explicit Transactions

For atomic multi-operation batches, pass an ITransaction to each write method. The changes are held in WAL memory and only flushed on commit. Disposing without committing automatically rolls back.

Basic Explicit Transaction

using var db = new AppDbContext("mydb.blite");

// Begin a transaction — ITransaction implements IDisposable
using var txn = db.BeginTransaction();

try
{
    // Pass txn to every write that must be atomic
    await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Alice", Age = 30 }, txn);
    await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Bob", Age = 25 }, txn);

    await txn.CommitAsync(); // or: await db.SaveChangesAsync(txn)
}
catch
{
    // Automatically rolled back on dispose if CommitAsync was not called
    throw;
}

Async BeginTransactionAsync

using var txn = await db.BeginTransactionAsync();

try
{
    await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Charlie" }, txn);
    await db.Users.UpdateAsync(existingUser, txn);

    await txn.CommitAsync();
}
catch
{
    await txn.RollbackAsync();
    throw;
}

When to Use Explicit Transactions

  • ✅ Two or more writes that must succeed or fail together
  • ✅ Complex multi-step operations with conditional logic
  • ✅ Operations spanning multiple collections with dependencies
  • ✅ When you need to roll back based on business logic

Comparing Auto-commit vs Explicit

⚡ Auto-commit (default)

Best for:
  • Independent inserts, updates, deletes
  • Bulk operations via InsertBulkAsync
  • Rapid development and simple CRUD
// Each write commits immediately
await db.Users.InsertAsync(user1);
await db.Users.InsertAsync(user2);

🔧 Explicit Transactions (BeginTransaction)

Best for:
  • Atomic multi-write batches
  • Complex business logic with conditionals
  • Cross-collection atomic operations
  • Fine-grained rollback control
using var txn = db.BeginTransaction();
await db.Users.InsertAsync(user, txn);
if (condition) await txn.CommitAsync();
else await txn.RollbackAsync();

Batch Operations with Explicit Transactions

Perform a delete-then-insert atomically:

using var txn = await db.BeginTransactionAsync();

// Collect IDs to delete (reads are outside the transaction)
List<ObjectId> toDelete = await db.Users.AsQueryable()
    .Where(u => u.Age > 60)
    .Select(u => u.Id)
    .ToListAsync();

foreach (var id in toDelete)
    await db.Users.DeleteAsync(id, txn);

// Insert new batch atomically with the deletes
await db.Users.InsertBulkAsync(newBatch, txn);

await txn.CommitAsync();

Error Handling

using var txn = db.BeginTransaction();

try
{
    await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Alice" }, txn);
    await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Bob" }, txn);

    await txn.CommitAsync();
}
catch (ValidationException ex)
{
    // Rolled back automatically on dispose
    Console.WriteLine($"Validation failed: {ex.Message}");
}
catch (IOException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"I/O error: {ex.Message}");
}

Explicit Rollback

Call RollbackAsync() to explicitly discard all changes in a transaction:

using var txn = db.BeginTransaction();

await db.Users.InsertAsync(new User { Name = "Test" }, txn);

if (someCondition)
{
    await txn.RollbackAsync(); // Discard changes
    return;
}

await txn.CommitAsync();

CancellationToken Support

All async operations accept an optional CancellationToken:

var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));

try
{
    using var txn = await db.BeginTransactionAsync(cts.Token);

    await db.Users.InsertBulkAsync(largeDataset, txn, cts.Token);
    await txn.CommitAsync(cts.Token);
}
catch (OperationCanceledException)
{
    // Transaction automatically rolled back on dispose
    Console.WriteLine("Operation cancelled");
}

Transaction Isolation

BLite uses Read Committed isolation. Each read sees the last committed state; writes inside a transaction are not visible to other readers until commit.

// Reader sees committed data only
var user = await db.Users.FindByIdAsync(userId);   // reads last committed value

// Writer holds changes until commit
using var txn = db.BeginTransaction();
user.Age = 31;
await db.Users.UpdateAsync(user, txn);

// Another reader still sees Age = 30 until txn.CommitAsync() is called
await txn.CommitAsync();

Read-Only Operations

Queries are outside the transaction model and always read committed data:

using var db = new AppDbContext("mydb.blite");

// Async LINQ — no transaction needed
List<User> users = await db.Users.AsQueryable()
    .Where(u => u.Age > 25)
    .OrderBy(u => u.Name)
    .ToListAsync();

// Streaming — no transaction needed
await foreach (var u in db.Users.FindAllAsync())
    Process(u);

BLiteSession — Per-Connection Isolation v3.8.0

When a single BLiteEngine instance is shared across multiple concurrent clients (e.g. inside BLite.Server), BLiteSession provides per-connection isolated transaction contexts. Each session carries its own transaction state so independent callers cannot interfere with each other.

Open a session with engine.OpenSession(). Disposing the session automatically rolls back any uncommitted transaction.

using var engine = new BLiteEngine("data.db");

// One session per connected client / per request
using var session = engine.OpenSession();

// Explicit transaction on this session
using var txn = session.BeginTransaction();

try
{
    await session.InsertAsync("orders", orderDoc, ct);
    await session.InsertAsync("invoices", invoiceDoc, ct);
    await session.CommitAsync(ct);
}
catch
{
    session.Rollback(); // or disposed automatically
    throw;
}

// Convenience CRUD without explicit transaction (auto-commit)
BsonId id = await session.InsertAsync("users", userDoc, ct);
BsonDocument? doc = await session.FindByIdAsync("users", id, ct);

// Access a collection scoped to this session
var col = session.GetOrCreateCollection("events");
await col.InsertAsync(eventDoc, ct);
💡 When to use BLiteSession
  • ✅ Server mode — one session per client connection ensures transaction isolation
  • ✅ Shared engine — multiple concurrent callers on a single BLiteEngine
  • ✅ Dispose-safe — uncommitted transactions are rolled back automatically on disposal
  • ⚠️ Embedded single-process apps — not required; use DocumentDbContext or BLiteEngine directly

Hot Backup (v1.8.0)

Create a consistent, online backup of the database without stopping or pausing the engine. Concurrent reads and writes remain safe during the copy.

// Typed API (DocumentDbContext)
using var db = new AppDbContext("mydb.blite");
await db.BackupAsync("backups/mydb-2026-06-06.blite");

// Schema-less API (BLiteEngine)
using var engine = new BLiteEngine("mydb.blite");
await engine.BackupAsync("backups/mydb-2026-06-06.blite");

The backup file is a standalone, fully consistent database that can be opened directly with a new engine instance.

How it works:
  • Acquires the commit lock (no new commits during copy)
  • Checkpoints WAL into the PageFile
  • Copies the PageFile to the destination path
  • Releases the lock — writes resume immediately
  • WAL is not copied — the destination is already consistent
// With CancellationToken support
var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
await db.BackupAsync("backup.blite", cts.Token);

Best Practices

  • ✅ Use auto-commit for independent single writes — simpler and sufficient
  • ✅ Use explicit transactions when two or more writes must be atomic
  • ✅ Always pass txn to every write that must be part of the transaction
  • ✅ Always use using on transactions to guarantee rollback on exceptions
  • ✅ Keep transactions short to minimize WAL pressure and lock contention
  • ✅ Pass CancellationToken for long-running operations
  • ✅ Use BLiteSession when multiple tasks share a single engine instance
  • ⚠️ Don't nest transactions — BLite uses a single active transaction per context
